review_notes: I read the whole file and the related definitions in Def_AdicCompletionTensorRing, Def_AdicCompletionRingFunctoriality, Def_StabilizerCompletionAction, Def_CompletionInvariants and Def_SemilocalAdicCompletion. I looked for missing simp lemmas, orientation problems, competing rules and possible loops. The only @[simp] in the target is transportOf_of, which is oriented correctly. completionBaseChangeHom_eq_tensor is correctly left non-simp, because tensorRingHom_tmul (simp) would rewrite its right-hand side back, giving a possible loop. The findings are about missing simp coverage and are not experimentally verified, since I could not run Lean. I did not check the exact statement or proof of the suggested lemmas by compiling them. The shapes suggested follow existing lemmas in the dependencies.

findings.problem: invariantsCompletionHom is a plain noncomputable def, so simp cannot see through it, and no simp lemma describes its action. The only lemma about its value is the evalₐ/mk form, which is not simp. The sibling maps have the canonical simp lemmas: completionBaseChangeHom_of and transportOf_of are @[simp], and evalₐ_of is simp in Mathlib. But there is no `invariantsCompletionHom (of 𝔭 A a) = of 𝔓 B (algebraMap A B a)`. The `of` form is the usual simp-normal generator form. Callers must re-derive it through evalₐ and ext_evalₐ, as stabAut_invariantsCompletionHom does.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] theorem invariantsCompletionHom_of (a : A) : invariantsCompletionHom A B G 𝔭 𝔓 (of 𝔭 A a) = of 𝔓 B (algebraMap A B a)`. Prove it with ext_evalₐ plus the existing evalₐ_invariantsCompletionHom. Alternatively unfold the def and use completionBaseChangeHom_of and semilocalComponent_of. Mark semilocalComponent_of @[simp] too, since it is currently not simp. Also mark evalₐ_invariantsCompletionHom @[simp], so that evalₐ of the image of `mk` reduces to the quotient class of `algebraMap A B (a.val n)`.
findings.benefit: Computations with the image of the map would go through simp. It would also match the existing @[simp] conventions on completionBaseChangeHom_of and transportOf_of. The repeated manual `show ... ; rw [semilocalComponent, ...]` unfolding would no longer be needed.

findings.problem: semilocalComponent and transportOf are defs defined through mapₐ, and simp does not unfold them. The file has no hypothesis-free simp lemma for `evalₐ Q n (semilocalComponent I hQ x)` or `evalₐ Q n (transportOf g h x)`. Instead it has lemmas that need a chosen representative `z` with an `hz` hypothesis. As a result the same unfolding `rw [semilocalComponent, evalₐ_mapₐ, ← hz, levelMapₐ_mk]; rfl` is repeated in at least four proofs (about lines 135, 143, 250, 324 and 335). evalₐ_component is stated at line 329, after semilocalComponent_selfSmul and evalₐ_invariantsCompletionHom, which could have used it. The hz-style lemmas cannot be used as simp lemmas, because `z` and `hz` are not determined by the left-hand side.
findings.proposed_change: Add simp lemmas that mirror the existing @[simp] evalₐ_mapₐ and levelMapₐ_mk. One is `evalₐ Q n (semilocalComponent I hQ x) = <levelMapₐ for AlgHom.id applied to> (evalₐ I n x)`. The other is `evalₐ Q n (transportOf A B G g h x) = levelMapₐ 𝔓 Q (MulSemiringAction.toAlgEquiv A B g : B →ₐ[A] B) _ n (evalₐ 𝔓 n x)`. Both are proved by `evalₐ_mapₐ`, so the left-hand side shrinks to a single `evalₐ`. Then evalₐ_component and evalₐ_transportOf follow from the new lemma plus `← hz` and `levelMapₐ_mk`. The unfolding proofs elsewhere can be replaced by a call to the new lemma.
findings.benefit: Removes the repeated unfolding boilerplate. A representative-free evalₐ lemma works with simp, whereas a lemma with `z` and `hz` hypotheses cannot be used by simp. Ordering the hypothesis-free lemma first lets later lemmas use it.

findings.problem: The equivalence is built with AlgEquiv.ofBijective on a codRestrict, and no coercion or apply simp lemma is provided. The same holds for invariantsCompletionRingEquiv. A user who has `(invariantsCompletionEquiv A B G 𝔭 𝔓 x : AdicCompletion 𝔓 B)` has no simp rule to turn it into `invariantsCompletionHom A B G 𝔭 𝔓 x`. So the file's other simp lemmas (completionBaseChangeHom_of, transportOf_of, and the invariantsCompletionHom_of proposed above) cannot be reached through the equivalence. Also, mem_fixedPoints_iff (line 467) is proved by Iff.rfl, but its statement embeds letI/haveI instance data and is not simp. The instance-heavy form makes it awkward as a rewrite rule.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] theorem coe_invariantsCompletionEquiv (x : AdicCompletion 𝔭 A) : ((invariantsCompletionEquiv A B G 𝔭 𝔓 x : FixedPoints.subalgebra ..) : AdicCompletion 𝔓 B) = invariantsCompletionHom A B G 𝔭 𝔓 x := rfl`, with the instances supplied as in the def. Add an analogous lemma for invariantsCompletionRingEquiv. Keep mem_fixedPoints_iff as a plain non-simp bridge lemma, or state it with the instances as arguments. Keep the simp normal form on the invariantsCompletionHom side.
findings.benefit: Gives the equivalence the standard apply/coe simp interface for ofBijective-built equivalences. Statements about the fixed-point subalgebra can then be reduced to statements about invariantsCompletionHom, and from there to `of`.
